title: Centralize admin & invite policy engine for org/team management
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Build a single, centralized invite policy engine that enforces org- and team-level invite rules (domain verification, email allowlist/denylist, SSO tenant constraints) and emits comprehensive audit events. The engine should be the single source of truth for invite decisions across the Console, REST API, CLI, and SAML provisioning flows.

Background: Currently invite checks are scattered between the front-end, a couple of auth middleware layers, and SSO-specific code paths. This has resulted in inconsistent behavior (e.g., allowlisted domains bypassing SSO checks, team-level denylist not applying to invites from admin UI), gaps in audit logging, and complicated RBAC v2 integration.

Scope & Acceptance Criteria:
- Centralized policy evaluation service (Invite Policy Engine, IPE) that accepts an invite request and returns an allow/deny + matched-rule metadata within 20ms p95 for typical org policies.
- Policy primitives supported: verified_domain_required, org_email_allowlist, org_email_denylist, team_email_allowlist, team_email_denylist, sso_enforcement (force-sso), require_verified_identity (for SAML assertion), allow_external_collaborators flag.
- RBAC mapping: only roles with invite permission in RBAC v2 can create invites; team owners may opt into team-level override rules.
- Audit log events for every invite lifecycle action: invite_created, invite_sent, invite_accepted, invite_revoked, policy_evaluated (with rule id and decision). Logs must include actor id, target email, org_id, team_id (if applicable), rule id, timestamp, and API surface (console/api/saml/prov).
- Admin Console UI: new "Invite policies" page under Org Settings with controls for allowlist/denylist entries, domain verification state, and per-team policy overrides.
- API: POST /orgs/{org}/invite-check (dry-run) and POST /orgs/{org}/invites should call IPE; errors must be explicit (400 for policy violation with code and message).
- SAML/SCIM integration: provider-configurable behavior when SSO enforced: either block invites for emails not covered by SAML assertion domains or mark as pending until IdP provisioning occurs.
- Backwards-compatible rollout: existing orgs remain in current permissive mode until opt-in; a migration job will scan for orgs with allowlist/denylist entries and propose a conservative policy import.

Design notes / Proposed approach:
1) New internal service: invite-policy-engine (library + small service layer). Expose EvalInvite(request) -> {decision: allow|deny|challenge, matched_rules: [ids], reasons: [strings]} and an audit helper to write a structured audit event. Implement as Go library used by API server and a lightweight HTTP endpoint for non-Go consumers.
2) Data model: policy records stored in the metadata DB with policy_scope = org|team and type = allowlist|denylist|domain_verify|force_sso. Rules have precedence: team override > org policy > global defaults.
3) Domain verification: add domain ownership verification tokens + DNS TXT flow (existing verification system is used), surface verified domains in IPE. If org has force_sso and SAML tenant has configured assertion_domains, evaluation should intersect allowed domains.
4) RBAC v2 integration: Invite API checks "invites:create" permission in RBAC v2. For team invites, also check team-level invite permission. IPE returns a flag that indicates whether the invite action requires an admin approval flow.
5) Audit logging: Use structured audit sink (events written to audit-log service S3/BigQuery) with schema version. Include raw policy snapshot in a separate storage bucket for forensic purposes.
6) Console/UI: a React admin page that shows policy rules, allows CSV upload for allow/deny lists, and a UI preview that runs a dry-run evaluation for a sample list of emails. Changes should be gated by a confirmation modal and recorded in audit logs.

Migration & Rollout:
- Phase 1 (alpha): internal orgs + security-testing orgs. Feature off by default.
- Phase 2 (beta): opt-in for customers via feature flag; provide migration tool and UI to preview imported rules.
- Phase 3 (GA): default enforcement for new orgs; existing orgs must opt-in or be migrated after 30-day notice.

Monitoring & Metrics:
- Invite policy decision latency histogram (p50/p95/p99), policy rejection rate per org, number of invites requiring manual approval, SSO-enforced invite rejections.
- Alert if policy evaluation p95 > 50ms or if rejection rate spikes by >3x for any org.

Security & Compliance:
- All changes require security_review_required and design review with IAM team. Audit events retention must satisfy compliance (90 days standard, configurable).
- Edge case: invites to role-based emails (info@, admin@) should be flagged for manual review if denylist/allowlist rules conflict.

Risks & Open Questions:
- Performance: ensure policy eval does not add significant latency for high-throughput orgs; consider caching policy snapshots in memory with TTL.
- SCIM provisioning / SAML IdP behavior for pending invites: should we auto-accept when SCIM creates the user? Proposed: accept if SCIM user creation event matches invite email and identity mapping is verified.
- Granularity: do we allow per-team denylist disallowing a user who is allowed at org-level? Current proposal: team denylist overrides org allowlist for invites to that team.

Deliverables / Acceptance Tests:
- Unit tests covering policy precedence and rule types.
- End-to-end tests: console flow, API dry-run, SAML flow for force-sso enabled org.
- Load test demonstrating 10k invite evals/sec with p95 < 100ms on standard instance (for autoscale planning).
- Manual security review and a short confluence playbook for incident handling if invite abuse is detected.
